card.name: Kandeka
card.tagline: Kunene stick-fighting and slap-boxing ringed by song
card.profile: Kandeka (also Khandeka) is a martial tradition of the Kunene people of southern Angola encompassing stick-fighting, slap-boxing and a war-dance display, documented by M. Thomas J. Desch-Obi (Wikipedia). At parties and festivals, particularly before engolo matches, public ritual slap-boxing took place in dance circles: an outer ring of community members kept a clapped rhythm and call-and-response song while fighters entered, raising open hands as a challenge. António Nogueira described kandeka stick duels among the Humbe in the 1850s as a means of conflict resolution.
card.insight: Kandeka is cited as one of the Angolan combat-dance traditions (with engolo) from which Afro-Brazilian capoeira is believed to derive, illustrating how martial movement, music and dance circles travelled the Atlantic with enslaved Angolans.
